name: plaid-bank-digest
description:
One connected bank (a Plaid Item) reduced to what a weekly money summary needs. Read-only: POSTs to Plaid's read endpoints (`/transactions/get`, and `/accounts/get` when transactions cannot be read); nothing is written and nothing is stored between runs. Returns `accounts` with balances, `cash` (depository accounts: the available balance, else the current one), `owed_on_cards`, and `transactions`: per-week totals counted back from yesterday (`day_to_day`, `fixed` = housing, utilities and loan payments, `income`), the same per category, last week's five largest items, the charges that repeat monthly at one price (`recurring`) and the ones seen for the second time last week (`new_recurring`, with `price_change` when the same merchant charged a different amount the month before). Transfers between accounts and credit-card payments are left out of spending and reported separately. A balance that could not be read is `null`, never 0. When transactions cannot be read (history still loading) `transactions` is `null`, the reason is under `unavailable` and the balances are still returned; when the bank cannot be read at all the node fails with Plaid's error code. Account numbers and their last digits are not returned. Use one node per bank and combine them with `plaid-money-summary`.

The module never holds a credential: ACCESS_TOKEN is a vault:// reference and the app's Plaid credentials are read from the vault by the host when the request is sent.

PLAID_ENV.description: The Plaid environment the bank was connected in. There is no default.

ACCESS_TOKEN.description: The vault reference of one connected bank's access token: 'vault://plaid/access_token/{item_id}'. Each bank connected from Settings has its own; list_secrets shows them with the bank's name. Anything other than this reference is refused, so a token can never be pasted here.

INSTITUTION.description: The bank's name as it should appear in the output (e.g. 'Wells Fargo').

TIME_ZONE.description: IANA zone name (e.g. 'America/New_York') whose local date decides 'today'. Weeks are counted back from yesterday in that zone. An unknown zone is an error.

WEEKS.description: How many weeks of transactions to read. Thirteen gives three charges of a monthly subscription.

TODAY.description: A fixed date (YYYY-MM-DD) to use instead of the clock. For tests.

setup_instructions.title: Connect the bank
setup_instructions.detail: Set PLAID_ENV, PLAID_CLIENT_ID and PLAID_SECRET on the controller (docs/plaid-setup.md), then connect each bank from Settings > Integrations > Bank accounts. The controller stores each bank's access token at 'plaid/access_token/{item_id}' and the app credentials at 'plaid/client_id' and 'plaid/secret'.

setup_instructions.title: Use a restricted actor
setup_instructions.detail: Bind the workflow to an actor with max_llm_tier 'tier1' and egress_scope 'public' (bank data can then reach no outside model), max_write_ceiling 'readonly' and http_verb_ceiling 'write' (Plaid's reads are POSTs; nothing else the actor does may change anything).

setup_instructions.title: One node per bank
setup_instructions.detail: Add one node per connected bank with PLAID_ENV, ACCESS_TOKEN 'vault://plaid/access_token/{item_id}', INSTITUTION and TIME_ZONE. Set continue_on_error on each so one bank that needs reconnecting does not hide the others, join them with a Collect node and follow it with 'plaid-money-summary'. These are reads, so an explicit retry_count of 1 or 2 is safe.
